subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Turkish Coffee: Sand, Cezve, and Fortune
description: A micro-lesson that makes Turkish Coffee: Sand, Cezve, and Fortune usable.

hook.text: Turkish coffee is brewed by boiling ultra-fine grounds in a small brass pot called a cezve—sometimes nestled in hot sand.

buildup.text: The grounds are never filtered. They settle to the bottom of tiny cups, creating a thick, sludgy bed of sediment.

discovery.text: That sediment is used for tasseography—fortune telling. The cup is inverted and patterns are read for the future.

twist.text: UNESCO added Turkish coffee to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2013. It's a world civilization.

climax.text: A Turkish proverb says: 'A cup of coffee commits one to 40 years of friendship.' Coffee is a social contract, not just a beverage.

punchline.text: Sand-brewed, unfiltered, fortune in the mud. Turkish coffee is pure ritual.

quiz.question: What is tasseography in Turkish coffee culture?
options: Fortune telling by reading patterns in the coffee sediment left in the cup
